title: Modelling Framework for the Estimation of Salmonid Abundance
text: Create factor pass separate levels first subsequent passes. NOTE: Assuming second third pass capture probability avoids problems model identifiability (Millar et al., 2016) Create sampleID grouping EF counts together. sample unique combination site visit x species x lifestage required EF function Create visitID unique site visits. required overdispersion function (see ). Create factor year
code: ef_data$pass12 <- factor(replace(ef_data$pass, ef_data$pass > 2, 2)) ef_data$sampleID <-   as.numeric(     factor(       paste(ef_data$date, ef_data$siteID, ef_data$lifestage, ef_data$species)     )   ) ef_data$visitID <- factor(paste(ef_data$date, ef_data$siteID)) ef_data$fyear <- factor(ef_data$year)

title: Modelling Framework for the Estimation of Salmonid Abundance
text: Fit simple model. contains factor pass (2 levels), lifestage (2 levels), site (3 levels) year (5 levels). larger dataset also possible add continuous variables linear smoothed terms providing degrees freedom specified (typically k=3 (2 d.f.), see Millar et al., 2016 details)
code: m1 <-   efp(     count ~ siteID + fyear + pass12 + lifestage,     data = ef_data, pass = pass, id = sampleID   ) ##  ## Call: ## efp(formula = count ~ siteID + fyear + pass12 + lifestage, data = ef_data,  ##     pass = pass, id = sampleID) ##  ## Formula: ## count ~ siteID + fyear + pass12 + lifestage ##  ## No random effects ##  ## Coefficients: ##                Estimate Std. Error  z value Pr(>|z^2|) ## (Intercept)    0.652301     0.1723  3.78656  1.527e-04 ## siteIDSite2    0.074540     0.1354  0.55059  5.819e-01 ## siteIDSite3   -0.023719     0.1473 -0.16098  8.721e-01 ## fyear2012     -0.209949     0.1736 -1.20936  2.265e-01 ## fyear2013      0.046976     0.1855  0.25317  8.001e-01 ## fyear2014      0.358431     0.1834  1.95389  5.071e-02 ## fyear2015     -0.004013     0.2114 -0.01899  9.849e-01 ## pass122       -0.239160     0.1311 -1.82436  6.810e-02 ## lifestageParr  0.590641     0.1210  4.88208  1.050e-06 ##  ## Degrees of Freedom: 90 Total (i.e. Null);  81 Residual ## AIC: 3188

title: Modelling Framework for the Estimation of Salmonid Abundance
text: model needs reformatted allow predictions (.e. obtain P) capture probabilities, uses .gam function. Predict P model full dataset. Note, data multi-pass can just use fitted values. However, want P single multi-pass data predict new dataframe
code: m1_gam <- as.gam(m1) ef_data$prob <- predict.gam(m1_gam, newdata=ef_data, type = "response")

what: Obtain Cumulative Estimates of P (for estimation of densities later)
title: Modelling Framework for the Estimation of Salmonid Abundance
text: Aggregate counts sampleID (.e. counts fry parr per site visit) Reshape get capture probability species x lifestage x site visit x pass. facilitates summary P. Get cumulative capture probability sampleID (see Glover et al., 2018) Remove individual pass capture probabilities Remove pass pass-specific data dataframe Join data cumulative counts sampleID Join data cumulative capture probability sampleID
code: counts <- aggregate(count ~ sampleID, ef_data, sum) probs <- cast(ef_data, formula = sampleID ~ pass, value = "prob") probs $ prob <- apply(probs[,2:4], 1, function(x) 1 - prod(1-x)) probs <- select(probs, sampleID, prob) densdata <- unique(select(ef_data, -count, -prob, -pass, -pass12)) densdata <- left_join(densdata, counts, by = "sampleID") densdata <- left_join(densdata, probs, by = "sampleID")

title: Modelling Framework for the Estimation of Salmonid Abundance
text: Density (N/m-2) estimated countsarea*P\frac{counts}{area*P} want model counts directly (Poisson model), need cumulative P area offset. Poisson model offset log⁡(area*cumulativeP)\log({area*cumulativeP}). Plot check
code: densdata $ Density_Estimate <- densdata $ count / (densdata $ area *                                                       densdata $ prob) densdata $ offset <- log(densdata $ area * densdata $ prob)

title: Modelling Framework for the Estimation of Salmonid Abundance
text: electrofishing count data typically overdispersed modelling framework incorpororate random effects, necessary estimate amount overdispersion data account comparing models. Overdispersion estimated fitting large model captures systematic variation data comparing visit-wise saturated model (see Millar et al., 2016): Use overdispersion function ef package specify data, visit ID, site ID, sample ID large model. View overdispersion estimate. ‘disp’ column contains estimates within sample overdispersion. largest values used adjust BIC. Compare models using adjusted BIC function (Equation 4, Millar et al., 2016) Full model Model without lifestage
code: large_model <- efp(count ~ fyear + pass12 + lifestage,                    data = ef_data, pass = pass, id = sampleID) od_estimate <- overdispersion(data = ef_data, visitID = "visitID",                               sampleID = "sampleID",                               control = list(maxit = 100),                               largemodel = large_model) ## Saturated model start time 2023-10-10 17:02:30.602148  ## Saturated model duration = 0 secs  ## Site visit model start time 2023-10-10 17:02:30.800149  ## Site visit model duration = 0 secs od_estimate ##                llik nparam deviance df      disp          p ## saturated -1552.715     60       NA NA        NA         NA ## sitevisit -1579.952     22 54.47317 38 1.4335045 0.04057796 ## large     -1585.472      7 11.04111 15 0.7360738 0.74967497 mfull <- efp(count ~ siteID + year + lifestage + pass12,              data = ef_data, pass = pass, id = sampleID)  BICadj(mfull, od_estimate) ## [1] 2235.949 mlife <- efp(count ~ siteID + year + pass12,              data = ef_data, pass = pass, id = sampleID)  BICadj(mlife, od_estimate) ## [1] 2250.261
